why: Both moved the same single piece of real traffic (the one shared OpenAI client behind /v1/chat/completions) with the same care about what must stay — Groq, the LiteLLM sidecar, Ollama, the model probes, and the browser client that points at the app's own origin — so the migration is a tie and the decision rests on the system-level work, where A is far deeper: it found and fixed the three real defects in this app (the `4096 - input_tokens` output cap that goes negative on a large refine, the chunk-counting quota with its `20 if "gpt-4" in model` substring bug that charged the cheapest model 20x, and the 2024-frozen picker), and settled model choice with live side-by-side runs through Router on OpenUI's own system prompt rather than from the catalog. B's two improvements are correct but small, and it demoted the most user-visible bug in the app to a note (n1) that explicitly blocks its own best idea — offering the gpt-5/6 models Router serves — instead of spending nine lines to unblock it.
A_best: Measured, ranked system judgment with real Router leverage: six validated branches, the negative-max_tokens fix, a price-weighted quota replaced by Router's reported usage and USD cost, and levers declined for measured reasons (Flex pinned off because a 25s queued stream in front of a watching user is a broken product; prompt_cache_key measured at +46% on 4o-mini and -24% on haiku).
B_best: Real test discipline — 14 passing against a 4-passing baseline, including a stubbed drive of the handler asserting the quota multiplier per model — plus the sharpest single catch in either report: that get_openai_models() gates the whole OpenAI menu on an OpenAI probe, so a Router-key-only deployment can route generations it can never start, fixed with a correct Router-catalog intersection and three fallback paths.
A_worst: Its catalog claim looks wrong: it asserts gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4o and gpt-4-turbo are absent from Router's live catalog, but B's validation shows a live 200 on gpt-3.5-turbo through Router and all four listed by GET /v1/models — and that claim is part of the argument for i2. It also added no tests (4 passed, identical to baseline) and left the frontend edits untypechecked.
B_worst: Thin system-level reach: it diagnosed the 4096-token arithmetic and the reasoning-model incomplete-with-no-text failure exactly right and then shipped nothing for it, left the quota's chunk-counting bug untouched, patched the 20x multiplier with another substring test (`"mini" not in model`) rather than price, and accepted a two-year-stale model menu as the product surface.
